skill.name: canvas-design
skill.description: Create visual design philosophies and express them as polished PNG or PDF artwork with sparse text, typography, composition, and bundled font guidance.
skill.summary: Create design philosophies and polished static canvas artwork.
skill.author: Azeem-2

security_audit.summary: The license and Markdown backtick detections are false positives: they are OFL legal text and a code-formatted path, not system reconnaissance or shell execution. The bundled font binaries remain low-severity supply-chain risks because they are not text-scannable. I also found unconstrained external font download guidance and a fabricated user-feedback instruction in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Limit downloads to approved font repositories, require user confirmation, and record source URLs for every new font.
Document source provenance and checksums for each bundled font, or replace binaries with trusted package references.
Remove claims that the user already requested changes. Phrase the second pass as an internal quality review instead.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded External Font Download Instruction
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md tells the agent to download whatever fonts are needed. This can trigger network access and ingestion of untrusted binary font files without source limits.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction directly permits open-ended font downloads. The risk is contextual because trusted font sources could make this safe, but no such constraint is present.

semantic_findings.title: Fabricated User Feedback Instruction
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md states that the user already demanded a pristine museum-quality masterpiece. This can misrepresent user intent and pressure the agent into extra work without user consent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The line explicitly claims a prior user request that may not exist. It affects behavior rather than secrets or code execution, so the confidence and severity are moderate.

actual_capabilities: Creates a written design philosophy before visual production.
Guides one-page PNG or PDF artwork with sparse text.
Uses composition, color, scale, pattern, and typography as visual systems.
Supports multi-page visual sets when requested.
Includes bundled font assets and guidance for font selection.
limitations: Does not provide interactive editing controls or live previews.
Requires a capable image, PDF, or canvas execution environment.
May need user confirmation before downloading external fonts.
Cannot guarantee legal clearance for user-provided brands or references.

use_cases.title: Event Poster Design
use_cases.description: Turn an event brief into a polished poster with strong composition and limited text.

use_cases.title: Editorial Art Direction
use_cases.description: Create a visual philosophy that guides a magazine-style static artwork.

use_cases.title: Product Launch Visuals
use_cases.description: Produce a refined PNG or PDF concept for a launch announcement or campaign asset.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Poster
prompt_templates.prompt: Use canvas-design to create a single-page PNG poster for [event]. Use sparse text and a clear visual mood.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Design Philosophy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use canvas-design to write a design philosophy for [topic]. Focus on color, form, rhythm, and minimal typography.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Branded Art Piece
prompt_templates.prompt: Use canvas-design to create a PDF artwork for [brand or project]. Include a subtle reference to [concept] without explaining it.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a Multi-Page Visual Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Use canvas-design to create a three-page visual set for [theme]. Keep each page distinct while sharing one design philosophy.

output_examples.input: Create a poster for a quiet jazz listening night.
output_examples.output: A PDF poster with sparse type, abstract rhythm marks, muted color fields, and a short design philosophy.

output_examples.input: Design a launch image for a new productivity app.
output_examples.output: A PNG artwork with structured grids, careful typography, restrained color, and subtle visual references to focused work.

output_examples.input: Make a two-page art set about coastal memory.
output_examples.output: Two related PDF pages with different compositions, shared palette choices, and a concise philosophy document.

best_practices: Provide the topic, desired format, dimensions, and required text before generation.
Review the design philosophy before asking for final PNG or PDF output.
Confirm font sources when the work needs new downloaded typefaces.
anti_patterns: Do not request dense text documents when the goal is visual artwork.
Do not ask for copies of a living artist or protected brand style.
Do not allow arbitrary font downloads in restricted environments.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a design philosophy and static visual output, usually as PNG or PDF.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it make multi-page work?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for multi-page visual sets when the user requests them.

faq.question: Does it include fonts?
faq.answer: Yes. The package includes bundled font files and instructions for selecting typography.

faq.question: Is it safe to use external fonts?
faq.answer: Use trusted font sources, verify licenses, and avoid downloads in locked-down environments.

faq.question: Can it copy a famous artist style?
faq.answer: No. The skill asks for original design work and should avoid copying protected styles.
